about.title: Merced Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Merced who walk into a clinic or emergency room leave with the care they came for. Sometimes they don't. A missed diagnosis, a medication mix-up, or a surgical error can turn a treatable problem into a lasting one, and the person on the receiving end is left with questions nobody seems eager to answer. LawProactive exists for that moment. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Merced County residents with an independent attorney who handles medical malpractice claims, and those attorneys work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California's MICRA rules make these cases different from other injury claims: you generally have one year from when you discovered the harm, never more than three years from the injury, and you must give the provider 90 days' notice before filing. A qualified medical expert is nearly always needed to show the care fell below the accepted standard. A poor result by itself is not malpractice, but if you suspect something went wrong, a conversation costs nothing.

whyChoose.title: Why Merced Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: MICRA's Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally allows one year from the date you discovered the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself. Getting connected early protects that window.

items.title: The 90-Day Notice Is Handled Correctly
items.desc: Before a malpractice suit can be filed, the provider must receive 90 days' written notice of intent. An attorney in our network knows how that step affects your timeline.

items.title: Expert Review From the Start
items.desc: Nearly every malpractice claim in California needs a qualified medical expert to explain how the care fell short. The attorneys we connect you with build cases around that requirement rather than guessing.

items.question: I was hurt in a collision on G Street and the emergency room missed a fracture. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: It might be, but the details matter. Merced recorded 349 people injured in 246 injury collisions in 2025, and many of them passed through local emergency care; a missed injury becomes a potential malpractice claim only if a reasonably careful provider would have caught it and the delay caused additional harm. An attorney will typically have a medical expert review your records to answer that question. Until then, keep every discharge paper, imaging report, and follow-up note.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in medical malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year under MICRA. Economic losses like medical bills and lost wages are treated separately. An attorney can explain how the current figures apply to your situation without anyone promising a number.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. If an attorney reviews your Merced case and concludes it is a bad outcome rather than malpractice, you will not owe anything for that honest assessment.
